body:
related #31652
depends on #40356

## Problem

There is no per-UI stateful concept of "their" colorscheme, background, etc. This is because detected terminal backgrounds are recorded in global state.

## Solution

Now that terminal responses can be associated with the TTY UI channel that produced them,  the next natural step is to store the dark/light result on the associated UI (via `RemoteUI`). Do so in a new field in `nvim_list_uis`.

This PR **does not** change anything from the end-user pov, nor implement the "per-ui" options pipelines - it just creates a place for state. Two remote UIs attached to the same server _still_ share the same background & colorscheme.

comment_data.body:
We should make this function more generally useful and have it take `r`, `g`, `b` values and return a `UIBackground` value. We should parse the OSC 11 response in `ui_term_event` instead of here, and then pass in the parsed RGB values to this function.

That also keeps the terminal-related logic (i.e. parsing OSC11 codes) in the `ui_term_event` function, which is already explicitly a "terminal" function (keeps related concepts together).
As @justinmk [mentioned](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40388/changes#r3484280862), the UI background is not terminal specific, and we may want to use this for non-TUI UIs too.

I think @justinmk already made a similar comment but I don't think we need `detected` in the name here, can probably just make this `bg` honestly.


```suggestion
  UIBackground bg;
```
1 statement w/ zero nesting instead of 3 + nesting
